title: SDK Lightweight Provisioner walkthrough (draft)
content:
Purpose: quick, low-friction guide for engineers to try the Redwood SDK locally with the minimal provisioning layer (the "Light Provisioner"). This is intentionally opinionated: defaults target a 10-minute demo loop for polyglot clients (JS/Python).

Scope:
- Walkthrough covers: zero-config local start, quick sample app (echo/chat/embeddings), a tiny smoke test harness, and minimal telemetry signals to validate integration.
- Not covered here: production Dedicated/Private deployment steps, advanced CI integrations, or infra-scale tuning.

Why this exists (context):
- Engineers repeatedly stumble on environment mismatches (node/python runtimes, token env vars, network proxies).
- We need a reproducible, tiny surface that demonstrates core DX: API auth, streaming, error handling, and telemetry in <10 minutes.

High-level flow (10-minute path):
1) git clone github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples-lite
2) cd local-quickstart
3) ./light-provisioner up  # fetches a cached local dev image and runtime shim, exposes port 8080
4) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=local-demo-<token>
5) npm run start-js  OR  python -m quickstart.python_app
6) open http://localhost:8080/demo -> try sample prompts (echo, summarize, embed search)
7) ./light-provisioner smoke  # runs basic request/response and telemetry-checks

Key commands (explanations):
- light-provisioner up: creates a single-process shim (no Docker daemon required where possible). Pulls prebuilt runtime artifacts (quantized small model variants) from our internal artifact cache. Goal: near-zero wait.
- smoke: runs 3 canonical requests (chat streaming, embedding similarity, rate-limit retry) and verifies status codes + token usage counters.

Sample local SDK wiring (notes, high-level):
- JS: uses our SDK client with env-based config. The example starts a small express server which streams partial tokens to the browser.
- Python: minimal Flask app, demonstrates synchronous generation and async streaming via websockets.
- Both samples include a single telemetry hook that emits: request_id, model, seq_len, latency_ms, success/failure.

Telemetry expectations (minimal):
- Events emitted to local collector at http://localhost:8081/telemetry (collector spun up by provisioner).
- Smoke verifies presence of: first_token_latency_ms, total_tokens, model_name.
- Purpose: ensure customers see signal when switching models or enabling quantized variants.

Failure modes we've encountered (and mitigations):
- Missing API key -> clear error message with remediation: "set REDWOOD_API_KEY or use --dev-token".
- Streaming stalls due to older node websockets -> fallback to polled chunking in JS example.
- Local port conflicts -> provisioner picks next-available port and prints the URL.
- Proxy environments -> provisioner supports HTTP(S)_PROXY env vars and prints a short diagnostic if upstream fails.

Smoke tests (what they check):
- 200 on simple generation, response contains expected anchor text.
- Streaming path returns at least 3 incremental chunks over 500ms window.
- Embedding call returns vector length matching model spec.
- Telemetry collector received corresponding events (request_id matching).

Developer UX guardrails (recommendations for first iteration):
- Keep default model tiny (for speed) and call it out in UI.
- Show explicit cost meter in sample UI for "per-token" estimate (even if dev token is free).
- Provide a single toggle to switch to a slightly larger variant (to demo quality delta).
- Always surface a "show raw request/response" panel to encourage debugging.

Open questions / TODOs (for this draft):
- Do we provide a local offline K/V cache example? (Valuable for app dev but adds cognitive load.)
- Should provisioner automatically register a demo route on the developer console (opt-in)?
- Determine whether to include a pre-warmed canary path to demo latency SLOs.
- Decide default telemetry retention and whether the local collector persists across "up/down" cycles.

UX copy notes (for final doc):
- Error strings should be actionable. Example: instead of "401 Unauthorized" show "Missing valid REDWOOD_API_KEY. Run: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=... or visit /console to create a token."
- Keep log excerpts short and provide "why this matters" footnotes.

Rollout plan (opinionated):
- Phase 0 (this doc): internal dev-experiment release as "alpha" to eng-internal (link in linked_artifacts).
- Phase 1: widen to Solutions & SE teams, gather 20 quick feedback notes (telemetry on which steps fail most).
- Phase 2: polish into official quickstart, add a one-click web-hosted trial that runs the provisioner in a cloud sandbox.

Handy links and artifacts:
- local artifact cache index: (internal) https://artifacts.redwood.ai/local-provisioner/index
- example repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples-lite (branch: provisioner-demo)
- related Confluence: Provisioning Playbook (linked above)

Notes to self (informal):
- keep commands minimal, avoid Docker install step where possible.
- avoid heavy Windows-specific instructions for v0 — mac/linux only, add Windows notes later.
- include one sample that demonstrates streaming cancellation mid-response (useful for mobile UX).

Last checkpoints before turning into a polished doc:
- confirm the light-provisioner binary handles proxy envs and port fallback.
- get a final thumbs-up from platform-security on dev token scoping.
- build a tiny automated e2e that runs the smoke script on CI to prevent regressions.

If you want to iterate: leave comments inline (use the reviewer shorthand "@owner: why X?") and I'll fold into next pass.
